faq.a: Yes. Jim is happy to give free quotes and advice, and often quotes the same day — one customer's review describes getting a quote that night and the job done the next morning.

faq.q: What's the minimum charge once I sign up for a job?
faq.a: Usually four hours, plus the float. The float is a standard charge covering transport of the machine from the yard to your site and back again once the job is done.

faq.q: I'm putting in a pool. Why use Northern Beaches Earthmoving for the excavation?
faq.a: Savings can be made using one contractor for the pool excavation plus any additional works, rather than the pool company, which will only dig the pool itself.

faq.q: Do I need council or DA approval?
faq.a: You should check with your local council before undertaking excavation works.

faq.q: What is Dial Before You Dig, and is it my responsibility?
faq.a: It's a free service for locating underground utilities before excavation starts, at 1100.com.au. It's the customer's or builder's responsibility to identify where the utilities are before work begins.

faq.q: I want to dig a garage under my house, but it's all rock. Can you do this?
faq.a: Yes — Jim is experienced in all types of rock excavation, including tight, hand-dug rock jobs in confined spaces.

_source.aboutText: Northern Beaches Earthmoving is a proudly family-owned and operated business, serving the local community for over 25 years. As both the owner and operator, Jim Brigden is hands-on with every project. This personal approach means clients deal directly with him from the initial site visit through to completion of the job — ensuring honest communication, attention to detail, and a consistent, high quality result. Behind the scenes, Jim's wife Lynette plays a key role in running the business, managing all administration with care and efficiency. Together they are committed to delivering friendly, reliable service with values you'd expect from a true family-run company. Northern Beaches Earthmoving specialises in all types of residential excavation work, including driveways, rock excavation, pool and spa digs, detailed footings, house site preparation, sandstone block retaining walls, and rubbish or fill removal. No job is too small — just honest, hard work from a trusted local family business.
_source.statsBlock: Owner Operator. 21 years experience. From initial estimate or quote through to completion of job. Professional, reliable and friendly. Finds practical solutions to site problems. Good communication with owners, builders and tradesmen. Complies with Workcover and OHS requirements. Fully insured.
_source.photoNote: No stock or theme demo images found anywhere on the site — every image is the client's own job photo, served from their own wp-content/uploads folders (2013, 2016 and 2023). Reworked 2026-09-23 after review: the original build reused several photos across hero/statement/service/gallery slots (up to 3x each). Re-cropped and re-mapped so every hero, statement, aperture, owner, service and gallery slot shows a different photo, drawing on the fuller downloaded set (pool, Wahroonga/Turramura wall and loaded-truck shots) that was on disk but unused. The hero is now a brighter, wider crop of Manly-Sandstone-Block-Wall-1.jpg (3024x4032 original), cropped to the well-lit sawn-block corner with grass and gravel in frame — much higher contrast than the previous narrow, shadowed crop of the same photo, which now runs as a distinct gallery-only file. Several of the newly-used photos (Turramura, Wahroonga finished wall, Fairlight, curved-wall rock saw) are smaller native originals (500-640px wide, WordPress web copies) rather than full-resolution phone shots, so they are used at their native size for gallery/service thumbnails, not upscaled. Only four photos on the whole site reach 1600px+ natively (Manly-Sandstone-Block-Wall-1.jpg, IMG_2787.jpg, IMG_2792.jpg, IMG_2785.jpg) plus the 1200x1600 loaded-truck shot; those anchor the hero, statement, aperture and one large gallery slot. Nothing was upscaled.
